sections.composition:
I. Drava Dravyas (Liquid Ingredients) 

 Karanja Tvak Svarasa (Pongamia pinnata — Indian beech bark juice) — 160 ml 
 Changeri Svarasa (Oxalis corniculata — Indian sorrel juice) — 160 ml 

 II. Ghrita Dravya 

 Murchita Goghrita (Processed Cow’s Ghee) — 160 ml 

 III. Kalka Dravyas (Herbal Paste Ingredients) 

 Jatiphala (Myristica fragrans — Nutmeg) — 5 gm 
 Jatipatra (Myristica fragrans — Mace) — 5 gm 
 Bhringaraja (Eclipta alba — False daisy) — 5 gm 
 Ahiphena (Purified opium latex — Papaver somniferum) — 5 gm 
 Kutaja Bija (Holarrhena antidysenterica — Kurchi seeds) — 5 gm 
 Ativisha (Aconitum heterophyllum — Indian aconite) — 5 gm 
 Ajamoda (Apium graveolens — Celery seeds) — 5 gm 
 Shambuka Mamsa (Snail meat) — 5 gm 

 Method Of Preparation 
 First, the Kalka Dravyas are finely processed into a smooth paste. This kalka is mixed thoroughly with Murchita Goghrita (processed cow’s ghee) in a clean stainless steel vessel. Then, the Drava Dravyas (Karanja Tvak Svarasa and Cangeri Svarasa) are added to the mixture. The entire preparation is heated on mild fire following classical Sneha Paka Vidhi (medicated ghee preparation process) with continuous stirring. The process is continued until the aqueous portion evaporates and only the medicated ghrita remains in its original quantity. After achieving proper Sneha Siddhi Lakshanas (signs of completion of medicated ghee formation), the ghrita is filtered and stored in clean, wide-mouthed glass containers. 
 Method Of Use 
 Internal Administration

sections.indications:
Raktatisara (bloody diarrhea) 
 Pravahika (dysentery) 
 Arshas (hemorrhoids) 
 Grahani Roga (malabsorption syndrome) 
 Chronic loose stools with mucus or blood 

 Therapeutic Properties 
 Karanja Tvak (Pongamia pinnata) and Kutaja (Holarrhena antidysenterica) are main drugs for Atisara (diarrhea) and Pravahika (dystentry), known for their Grahi and antimicrobial properties. Jatiphala and Jatipatra (Myristica fragrans) provide strong Stambhana action, helping to reduce excessive bowel movements. Ativisha (Aconitum heterophyllum) improves digestion and controls pediatric as well as chronic diarrhea. Bhringaraja (Eclipta alba) supports liver function and aids in detoxification. Ahiphena (Papaver somniferum) contributes potent anti-diarrheal and analgesic effects. Changeri (Oxalis corniculata) enhances digestion and reduces intestinal inflammation. Goghrita acts as a soothing and nourishing base, promoting healing of intestinal mucosa and enhancing drug delivery.
sections.precautions:
Should be used strictly under medical supervision 
 Use cautiously due to presence of Ahiphena (opium derivative) 
 Avoid in pregnancy and children without guidance 
 Monitor for constipation or excessive dryness 
 Not suitable in severe Ama (endotoxins) conditions without prior Deepana (digestive) therapy 

 Conclusion 
 Punkintoladi Ghrita is a highly effective classical Ayurvedic formulation for managing Raktatisara (bloody diarrhea), Pravahika (dysentery), Arshas (Piles), and Grahani (malabsorption syndrome) disorders. Its unique combination of Grahi (absorbs excess fluid and controls diarrhea), Stambhana (arrests bleeding), and Deepana (digestive) herbs helps control diarrhea, reduce bleeding, and restore digestive balance. When used appropriately, it provides rapid relief and supports long-term gastrointestinal health.
